audit.armB.headline.method: 5-fold x 3 repeat CV, PCA-30 (random_state=42), scaled; value is the mean over 10 PCA seeds
audit.armB.headline.note: Seed-swept central estimate over 10 PCA seeds (sd 0.28 pp, range 67.1-67.9%). Supersedes the previously recorded 67.9%, which was a single draw from an UNSEEDED PCA: at 64x10240 sklearn selects the randomized SVD solver, so the figure was not reproducible (re-running the unmodified script gave 67.5%). PCA now carries random_state=42, making any single run reproducible; the quoted headline is the sweep mean, not one seed. Only this probe moved -- no-PCA, RBF, context-32d, the out-of-fold confusion matrix, per-class recalls and the attribution Wilcoxon p are all bit-identical to before.

audit.armB.headline.sd.note: Fold-level sd across the 15 CV folds at the default PCA seed -- NOT the PCA-seed sd (see audit.armB.headline.pca_seed_sd).

e0.armA.accuracy.ci_exact95.lower.method: Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95% lower bound (two-sided degenerates: Arm A is at the 100% ceiling, so only the lower bound is informative)

e0.armA.accuracy.ci_exact95.upper.method: trivial ceiling (80/80 correct), not a fitted bound

perception.accuracy.ds2.overall.note: deterministic full-DS2 eval of the ONE frozen checkpoint shared by both arms -- not a best-of-3 selection. The 84.9/80.1/85.4 range in edge_health_agent_kb.md describes variance across 3 separate TRAINING runs (different checkpoints); this figure is a single eval of the specific checkpoint actually in use, which happens to numerically coincide with that range's upper end. Report this checkpoint-specific number, not the training-time range. Also distinct from the Arm A/B urgency-tier accuracy (armA/B.accuracy.n80), which is scored on the 80-event subset against the reference tier, not the AAMI class.

perception.accuracy.ds2.s_recall_full.note: same figure as perception.accuracy.ds2.S, re-keyed for explicit contrast with s_recall_matched20 below

perception.accuracy.ds2.s_recall_matched.note: same figure as s_class.classifier_recall_matched; ci95 is documentation only (a list isn't independently {{...}}-renderable) -- use the .ci95.lower/.ci95.upper keys below in prose

e1.seeded_ablation.seed.note: shared training seed across all four k values in this specific curve. SCOPE OF CLAIM: controls ONE confound (uncontrolled initialization across k); does NOT give multiple seeds per k, so it cannot separate a genuine k-effect from seed-101-specific luck. E2 measured pure seed noise at fixed k=4 as std 8.7pp (ddof=1) / range 16.2pp -- same order as E1 adjacent-k deltas. Supportable claim: 'directionally consistent under a matched-seed check'. NOT 'accuracy depends on k'. Cite only in Results 4.6 / Discussion; never as headline accuracy.

e1.seeded_ablation.k4.note: reused from E2 seed=101, NOT the headline checkpoint. Do NOT confuse with armB.accuracy.n80 (95.0%) or e1.k4.accuracy (95.0%) -- those are the uncontrolled-seed headline that E0/auditability/norm-check are all anchored to, and it does not move. This 81.2% belongs ONLY to the matched-seed curve in 4.6.

audit.per_class.S.recall.note: Draw-dependent, and optimistic. Correct as reported for the headline 80-event selection, but that selection's S quarter comes from only 7 of the 16 S-containing DS2 records (up to 5 events each), and three of those records contribute a single event apiece that the probe recovers perfectly. Re-drawing the S quarter stratified across all 16 records (max 2/record, N/V/F quarters untouched, identical protocol) gives 45.0% -- see audit.s_redraw.per_class.S.recall. Report the 60.0% figure with this caveat rather than as a stable property of the representation.

s_class.per_record.new43.probe_mean.note: Four (219, 231, 233, 234) show 0%; three of four (219, 233, 234) have n=5 -- this low end is more solidly established than the 100% end above.

audit.armB.headline.pca_seed_sd.note: Reproducibility spread of the headline across PCA random seeds; distinct from the fold-level sd. Range 67.1-67.9%.

audit.s_redraw.per_class.S.recall.note: S-class recall under a stratified S redraw (round-robin across all 16 S-containing records, max 2/record vs the headline draw's 7 records / max 5). Directly comparable to audit.per_class.S.recall (60.0%): same probe, same CV protocol, same N/V/F quarters, only the S draw differs -- a 15.0 pp fall. Distinct from s_class.probe_recall_n63 (34.9%), which answers a different question (more S data) AND uses a mixed mechanism (existing CV out-of-fold for the original 20 plus single-fit predictions for 43 more), so it corroborates the direction but is not a like-for-like comparison.

audit.s_redraw.headline.note: Headline auditability recomputed with the stratified S redraw substituted in, mean over 10 PCA seeds. Moves -0.12 pp against audit.armB.headline (67.6%), i.e. 0.24x the combined PCA-seed noise -- no detectable change. The headline survives the redraw even though S-class recall does not: S loses 3 correct while N gains 1 and F gains 2, because the harder S events stop intruding on the N/F decision regions. Pooled out-of-fold accuracy is 68.8% either way.

audit.s_redraw.headline.delta_pp.note: Signed change in the headline under the stratified S redraw; compare against audit.armB.headline.pca_seed_sd as the noise floor.

audit.s_redraw.n_records.note: S-containing records represented in the redrawn S quarter (max 2 events each), versus 7 records (max 5 each) in the headline draw.
